title: fastpath: add gating and precision-toggle with safe-mode fallback for kernel/scheduler correctness
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: the fast-path kernels and scheduler optimizations provide large throughput wins for typical production workloads, but we observed edge-case correctness regressions when combinations of quantization, uncommon attention patterns, and aggressive KV cache reuse occur. This PR introduces a conservative gating mechanism for the fast-path, a runtime precision-toggle, and a safe-mode fallback that forces the reversion to the slow path on detection of potential correctness risk. Summary of changes: 1) runtime/core: introduce fastpath_gating policy that evaluates compatibility flags (model layout, quantization profile, token-length histogram) before selecting the fast-path kernel; 2) kernels/cuda: add precision_toggle hooks (fp16/amp/int8-aware codepaths) and small guarded checks to ensure reductions/accumulators don't overflow in corner cases; 3) scheduler: add a quick preflight pass that checks request batch characteristics (max_seq, attention pattern signatures, kv-cache hit rate) and annotates requests with gating decisions so routing is deterministic across micro-batches; 4) kvcache: add conservative KV cache validation when fastpath is selected so KV lookups are validated against model state hashes; mismatches trigger safe-mode; 5) continuous-batching: keep batching heuristics but add per-route override when safe-mode has been triggered recently; 6) telemetry: event+metric for fastpath_decisions, fastpath_fallback_reasons, precision_switches, and histogram of latency/cpu/gpu time for both paths; 7) tests: unit tests for gating logic, integration test injecting mismatched kv states, and microbench harness results with baseline numbers. Design notes and rationale: the gating logic is intentionally conservative to prioritize correctness in the first rollout-fastpath is allowed only when model quantization profile matches a verified list, sequence-length distribution is within expected bounds, and KV cache hash validation passes. The precision-toggle is exposed as a runtime knob (disabled by default on customer-controlled Dedicated/Private until the customer opts in) and the safe-mode will flip the route to the slow, verified path for the specific request/session to prevent regression propagation. Rollout plan: feature guarded behind runtime flag fastpath_gating.v1, staged rollout to internal clusters, then beta for a subset of Dedicated pools, monitor metrics for fastpath_fallback_rate and tail latency regressions. Checklist: - [x] implement gating and hooks - [x] add metrics/events - [x] unit/integration tests - [x] documentation and feature flag - [x] internal canary rollout notes Commits summary: 7 commits touching runtime core, scheduler, kernels, kvcache, tests, and docs. See commit_messages for details. CI: initial CI run failed on a flaky kernel test (reduction edge-case) then a guard was added to the kernel implementation and CI passed on rerun. Impact: adds 1) measurable throughput gains when fastpath is used (~+40% tokens/sec on standard long context workloads in microbench), 2) small added CPU overhead for gating checks (~1-3% latency increase on path selection), 3) robust fallbacks that eliminate previously observed correctness regressions. Backwards compatibility and safety: default behaviour on main remains unchanged until the feature-flag is enabled; Dedicated/Private customers must explicitly opt into precision-toggle. Related: references ENG-4281 and the perf canary tests in perf-canary repo. Merge: squash-merged after approvals and green CI.
commit_messages: introduce fastpath gating policy and config
add precision_toggle hooks to cuda kernels with guarded reductions
scheduler: preflight gating pass and request annotation
kvcache: add state hash validation and safe-mode trigger
release_notes: Add conservative fastpath gating and safe-mode fallback: fastpath enabled behind runtime flag; precision-toggle available as runtime opt-in; telemetry added for fastpath decisions and fallbacks.
